newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Pharma open to future acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: China Pharma open to future acquisitions.

text.p: The major shareholder of China Pharmaceutical Enterprise and Investment Corp Ltd said it will consider future asset injections into the unit after the recent purchase of a controlling stake in a major penicillin producer.

"The projects must have good market potential, products with good concepts, an investment return of not less than 20 percent, and not result in a dilution of earnings per share," Cai Dong Chen, chairman and general manager of Shijiazhung Pharmaceutical Group Corp, told a news conference in Hong Kong on Wednesday.

The company is currently in talks with a pharmaceutical manufacturer but has not as yet concluded any investment agreements, Wang Chun Yao, chairman of China Pharmaceutical Enterprise and Investment Corp Ltd, said at the news conference.

China Pharmaceutical, which is China's third largest manufacturer of vitamin C and the world's largest exporter of the vitamin, has just completed the acquisition of a controlling stake in its former associate Hebei Zhongkang Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.
Company shareholders earlier this month approved the company's raising its stake in Hebei Zhongkang to 99 percent from 26.01 percent.
China Pharmaceutical purchased the stake with the issue -- to parent Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical -- of 250.52 million new shares at HK$1.18 each for a total of HK$295.61 million.
The deal raised Shijiazhuang's stake in the company to 69.86 percent from 57.26 percent.
In 1995, Hebei Zhongkang contributed HK$3.90 million or 20 percent of China Pharmaceutical's reported profit after tax of HK$19.39 million.
Hebei Zhongkang is China's second largest manufacturer of bulk penicillin and for the eight months ended August 1996 had profits after tax of 69.57 million yuan.
The consensus forecast for China Pharmaceutical in 1996 is HK$40.3 million, an increase of 108 percent over 1995, and HK$49 million in 1997, an increase of 22 percent.
This acquisition should significantly increase China Pharmaceutical's production capabilities and revenues and diversify its earnings base, company officers said.
In 1997, the pencillin maker could contribute as much as 50 percent of the China Pharmaceutical group's revenue, said Rosetta Leung, financial controller of the listed company.
The company's results will also be boosted by a stabilisation in the price of vitamin C, company officials said.

Last year, a price war among the world's leading manufacturers drove the price of vitamin C below cost levels. Prices have since recovered by 10 percent to 15 percent after bottoming out in May 1996, company officers said.
The industry in China, which produces about one-third of the worldwide demand for vitamin C, has since gone through a shake out.
"Last year, there were 22 manufacturers of vitamin C in China. Now there are only eight left," said Cai Dong-chen, chairman and general manager of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Corp.
"China Pharmaceutical was one of the chief beneficiaries (of the shake out)," he added.
One of the main reason for the company's success is that its production cost of vitamin C is the lowest in the world, said Wong.
The share closed HK$0.02 higher at HK$1.10 on Wednesday.
